title: CueFlux prompt lab notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal lab for a small prompt-suite I call 'CueFlux' — focused on lightweight role cues + morphological anchors to reduce drift on behaviorally fragile tasks (few-shot classification, multi-step extraction).

Context / constraints:
- Running on hosted API baseline (gptx-small-ish) and a quantized private replica (q4).
- Tight token budget: target < 120 tokens per request for production candidates.
- Need robust behaviour when exemplar set order changes and when user query drops context tokens.
- Main failure modes observed so far: instruction echo, hallucinated attributes, label flip when negative exemplars present.

Notes-to-self (observational):
- Short cue words like "Anchor:" + 1-line descriptor seems to stabilize label alignment more than multi-sentence role blocks.
- Preferring concrete output schema ("OUTPUT: <json>") reduces hallucination but increases truncation risk.
- q4 model more prone to tokenization-sensitive flips (punctuation after label matters).

CueFlux prompt skeleton (minimal):
- System / top: "You are a concise extractor. Use the EXEMPLARS to map user text to the OUTPUT. If unsure, return \"UNKNOWN\". Always include \"confidence: LOW/MED/HIGH\"."
- Anchor cue: single-line label like "Anchor: sentiment-v1 (labels=positive|neutral|negative)"
- EXEMPLARS: 3 short shots, terse delimiting (---)
- USER: short input
- OUTPUT: strict one-line json map

Primary template (example):

SYSTEM: You are a concise extractor. Use the EXEMPLARS to map user text to the OUTPUT. If unsure, return "UNKNOWN". Always include confidence: LOW/MED/HIGH.
Anchor: intent-classify-v2 (labels=signup|support|billing|other)
EXEMPLARS:
---
User: I can't sign up, the button is greyed out
OUTPUT: {"label": "signup", "confidence": "HIGH"}
---
User: Where do I change my card?
OUTPUT: {"label": "billing", "confidence": "HIGH"}
---
User: The app crashes when I open it
OUTPUT: {"label": "support", "confidence": "MED"}
---

User: {input_text}
OUTPUT:

Few-shot variation notes:
- Swap positive/negative ordering in exemplars during A/B to detect label anchoring.
- Introduce 1 adversarial exemplar where label is ambiguous to force UNKNOWN behavior.

Concrete few-shot set (for debugging):
1) Clean shot (short):
User: How do I reset my password?
OUTPUT: {"label": "support", "confidence": "HIGH"}

2) Ambiguous shot:
User: I got charged twice for last month
OUTPUT: {"label": "billing", "confidence": "MED"}

3) Counterexample (intent mixing):
User: I want to cancel my subscription and move data elsewhere
OUTPUT: {"label": "support", "confidence": "LOW"}

Observed failure cases (recent runs):
- Label flip when the user sentence contains both signup and billing words: model picks the earlier token as label. Root cause hypothesis: lexical priority + exemplar ordering.
- Hallucinated fields: model produces extra keys like "next_step" when exemplar schema was loosely phrased.
- Truncation: long user messages with schema cause OUTPUT to be cut mid-json (timeout / token limit).

Small experiments & results (quick log):
- 2024-11-17: baseline template (no Anchor cue) on hosted -> accuracy 0.72 on 200-sample holdout, hallucination rate 8%.
- 2024-12-01: added Anchor line + strict OUTPUT header -> accuracy 0.81, hallucination 3%, avg tokens/request -8%.
- 2025-01-05: introduced adversarial exemplar -> robustness to ordering improved (stddev labels across shuffles dropped from 0.14 to 0.07).
- 2025-02-09: deployed q4 replicate -> 0.78 accuracy but observed punctuation-sensitivity: adding a trailing period after label in exemplars flips some predictions.

Hypotheses to try next:
- Make label tokens canonicalized with brackets, e.g., [billing] vs billing — test if token boundary helps q4.
- Replace explicit "confidence" strings with numeric scores (0-100) to see if model remains calibrated.
- Try 2-shot anchor variants: "Anchor: intent-classify-v2|short" vs multi-line.

Mini troubleshooting checklist (for SRE/dev testing):
- Re-run failing samples on host with debug flag to get token-level trace (ask infra for trace id).
- If truncation occurs, switch to compact schema: one-letter label mappings (b/s/n/o).
- For q4 punctuation flips, run tokenizer diffs and sweep exemplar punctuation variants.

Quick TODOs (priority):
- [ ] Run 1k-sample shuffle experiment with bracketed labels by 2025-02-20 (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Add a tiny deterministic post-checker that invalidates JSONs missing "label" key (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Draft short PR with examples for prompt-lab README (owner: Rina).

Loose ideas and riffs (brainstorm):
- Use a micro-schema language: "L:billing;C:HIGH" to force token compactness and remove punctuation variability.
- Fusion: combine short cue-anchor with a trailing human-readable hint like "If unsure, say UNKNOWN" to bias toward abstention.
- Move some exemplar variance into the system message instead of in-shot to reduce exemplar dependency.

Slack snippets I want to post for quick sync:
- "Running CueFlux: bracket labels cut punctuation sensitivity on q4 in my early tests. Ethan will run full sweep."
- "Obs: introducing single adversarial exemplar reduces label anchoring — worth defaulting one per candidate set."

Misc notes:
- Keep production token target <=120. Consider post-request compress/translate stage if output exceeds budget.
- Document all exemplar shuffles in the sample metadata (tag: shuffle-v1, v2, etc.).

End of scratchpad.
